newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Denko to buy into Mongolian oil reserve.
newsitem.headline: Denko to buy into Mongolian oil reserve.

text.p: Denko Industrial Corp Bhd said on Friday it was proposing to buy a 45 percent stake in NTI Resources Ltd, which owns part of a Mongolian oil reserve, for 42 million ringgit.

In a statement, the electrical and metal parts maker said NTI Resources owns 42.6 percent in SOCO Tamsag Mongolia Inc, the concession holder for 10.7 million acres of oil reserves in Mongolia's Tamsag Basin.
Denko said it will issue 5.68 million new shares valued at 7.40 ringgit a piece to Pacific Communications Ltd for the stake. Pacific Communications is the parent of NTI.
Subsequent to the deal, Pacific Communications will hold an estimated 11.5 percent interest in Denko.
The Tamsag reserves are estimated to hold about one to two billion barrels of recoverable oil and are expected to be commercial in three years.
Denko also said the acquisition opens up opportunities for it to enter the China market.
Shares of Denko were suspended on Friday pending a news announcement. The stock last traded at 17.70 ringgit.
Edward Soeryadjaya, chairman and chief executive officer of NTI, said NTI has already started preliminary active drilling in the area.
"The outlook is very positive. In fact, we are optimistic that quantifiable reserves will eventually exceed our current estimations," he told reporters following the signing.
Soeryadjaya said NTI plans to drill 40 wells by the year 2000, which will involve a total investment of $68 million.
He said SOCO Tamsag currently has a contract to sell all of its crude oil to state-owned China National Petroleum Co.
The Chinese firm will buy the oil at the Platt's average per barrel posted Daqing export price minus a transport allowance of $2.00.
Denko's executive chairman Nor Azah Awin said the NTI shares were acquired at a discount of about 60 Malaysian cents each to the current market price.
She said she did not expect any immediate impact on Denko's results, but added that the acquisition could enhance earnings in the future.
She also said Denko is seeking a waiver from Canadian regulatory authorities from making a general offer for the rest of NTI's shares that it does not own.
